# Docker client: image build, image and volume calls, and the fake Docker support for them

## What to build

graph-manager's own Docker Engine API client (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.ts`, no dependency, `node:http` over the unix socket, API `/v1.45`) gets the calls the new sandbox image builder needs: build an image from a tar context with a streamed log, inspect an image (its `Id` and `Config.Env`), list images by label, remove an image, create a volume with labels, list volumes by label, and remove a volume. The fake Docker used by the tests and the live tester (`apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs`) learns the same endpoints, so later slices can be tested without real Docker. Nothing calls the new methods yet; this slice is the foundation for the spec `docs/prd/sandbox-image.md` (read its "Docker client" requirements).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `docs/prd/sandbox-image.md` — the spec; section "Requirements → Docker client" and "Tests" (fake-docker bullet).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.ts` (whole file, ~276 lines) — `request()` (lines ~108–143) buffers the whole body; `pullImage` (lines ~254–269) parses a JSON-lines progress stream and throws the last `error` as `DockerError(500, …)`; `imageExists` (lines ~271–275) encodes an image name with `name.split("/").map(encodeURIComponent).join("/")`; `createVolume`/`inspectVolume` (lines ~244–253).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.test.ts` — the test pattern: start the fake with `startFakeDocker()`, build a `DockerClient(fake.socketPath)`, assert on `fake.requests` and the fake's maps.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tar.ts` — `tarArchive(entries: TarEntry[], owner: { uid; gid }): Buffer`, `TarEntry = { path; dir?; content?: Buffer; mode? }`; use it to build a context with a single `Dockerfile` entry in tests.
- `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs` (602 lines) — `startFakeDocker({ socketPath, exec, images, self })` (line ~102); `imageSet = new Set(images)` (line ~118); `handle()` (line ~308) parses tar bodies with `parseTar(raw)` into `tarEntries` (each `{ name, type, mode, data }`) and records `requests.push({ method, path, query, body })`; `startPassive(c)` (line ~293) marks a started container running forever; containers' `Mounts` entries are `{ Type, Name?, Source, Destination, RW }`; images section at the end of `handle()` (lines ~531–543); volumes section (lines ~515–529); the returned object (lines ~555–570) and the CLI entry (lines ~572–602) with flags `--exec` and `--image`.
- `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.d.mts` (if present) or the `FakeDocker` type imported by tests from `../../scripts/fake-docker.mjs` — keep the type in sync with any new returned field.

## Patterns to follow

**Request with accepted statuses** (docker.ts):
```ts
async inspectVolume(name: string): Promise<VolumeInfo | undefined> {
  const res = await this.request("GET", `/volumes/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, { ok: [404] });
  if (res.status === 404) return undefined;
  return JSON.parse(res.body.toString("utf8")) as VolumeInfo;
}
```

**Label filters** (docker.ts `listContainers`):
```ts
return this.json<ContainerSummary[]>("GET", "/containers/json", { query: { all: 1, filters: JSON.stringify({ label: [label] }) } });
```

**Stream errors** (docker.ts `pullImage`): Docker answers 200 and reports failure in the stream; read to the end, throw `new DockerError(500, message)`.

**Comments**: one short comment line per method, explaining the why; request bodies are never logged or put in errors.

**Fake handlers** (fake-docker.mjs): `sendJson(res, status, body)`, `sendEmpty(res, status)`, regexes on `p` (the path without the `/v1.45` prefix), `decodeURIComponent` on names.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export interface ImageInfo { Id: string; RepoTags?: string[]; Config?: { Env?: string[]; Labels?: Record<string, string> | null } }` and `export interface ImageSummary { Id: string; RepoTags: string[] | null; Labels?: Record<string, string> | null }`.
- **IMPLEMENT** a private helper `imagePath(name)` returning `name.split("/").map(encodeURIComponent).join("/")` and use it in `imageExists` too.
- **IMPLEMENT** `async inspectImage(name: string): Promise<ImageInfo | undefined>` — `GET /images/<imagePath>/json`, `ok: [404]`, undefined on 404.
- **IMPLEMENT** `async listImages(label: string): Promise<ImageSummary[]>` — `GET /images/json` with `filters: JSON.stringify({ label: [label] })`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `async removeImage(nameOrId: string): Promise<void>` — `DELETE /images/<imagePath>`, `ok: [404, 409]` (409 = in use by a container: skipped silently).
- **IMPLEMENT** `createVolume(name: string, labels?: Record<string, string>)` — body `{ Name: name, ...(labels ? { Labels: labels } : {}) }` (keep the existing callers working).
- **IMPLEMENT** `async listVolumes(label: string): Promise<VolumeInfo[]>` — `GET /volumes` with the label filter; Docker answers `{ Volumes: VolumeInfo[] | null, Warnings }`; return `Volumes ?? []`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `async removeVolume(name: string): Promise<void>` — `DELETE /volumes/<encodeURIComponent(name)>`, `ok: [404, 409]`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `async buildImage(tag: string, context: Buffer, opts: { nocache?: boolean; labels?: Record<string, string>; onLine?: (line: string) => void } = {}): Promise<void>` — `POST /build` with query `{ t: tag, nocache: opts.nocache ? 1 : 0, rm: 1, forcerm: 1, labels: opts.labels ? JSON.stringify(opts.labels) : undefined }`, body = `context` with content-type `application/x-tar`, timeout 30 minutes. It must stream: `request()` buffers everything, so add a private `streamRequest(method, path, opts, onChunk: (chunk: Buffer) => void): Promise<number>` (or an `onData` option on `request`) that hands each chunk to a JSON-lines splitter. Keep a partial-line buffer across chunks. For each complete line: parse JSON; if it has `stream` (string), split it on `\n`, `trimEnd()` each piece, and call `onLine` for non-empty pieces; if it has `errorDetail.message` or `error` (string), remember it. After the end: non-2xx status → `DockerError(status, errorMessage(...))`; a remembered stream error → `DockerError(500, message)`. Invalid JSON lines are ignored.
- **GOTCHA**: never include the request body in errors. Use the same timeout/destroy pattern as `request()`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs`

- **IMPLEMENT** an image store: replace `imageSet` (a `Set` of names) by a `Map` name → `{ Id: "sha256:<64 hex>", Labels, Env }`. Images passed with `images: [...]` / `--image` and pulled ones get `Labels: {}`, `Env: ["PATH=" + DEFAULT_PATH]`. Keep every existing behaviour (the `missing` pull failure, `GET /images/<name>/json` 404 for unknown names) and make `GET /images/<name>/json` answer `{ Id, RepoTags: [name], Config: { Env, Labels } }`, also when `<name>` is an image id (`sha256:…`).
- **IMPLEMENT** `POST /build`: the body is a tar (already parsed into `tarEntries`); find the entry named `Dockerfile` and read its text. Record `builds.push({ tag: query.t, nocache: query.nocache === "1" || query.nocache === "true", labels: JSON.parse(query.labels ?? "{}"), dockerfile })`. Answer 200 `application/json` as a JSON-lines stream: one `{"stream":"Step <i>/<n> : <line>\n"}` per non-empty Dockerfile line; if the Dockerfile contains `FAKE_BUILD_FAIL`, end with `{"errorDetail":{"message":"fake build failed"},"error":"fake build failed"}` and create no image; otherwise store the image under `query.t` with a NEW id every build (the old one keeps nothing pointing to it), `Labels` from the query, `Env` = `["PATH=" + DEFAULT_PATH]` plus, for each Dockerfile line starting with `ENV PATH=`, `PATH=<value with $PATH replaced by DEFAULT_PATH>` instead, then write `{"aux":{"ID":"<id>"}}` and `{"stream":"Successfully tagged <tag>\n"}`. Support an optional build delay: a new option `buildDelayMs` (CLI flag `--build-delay <ms>`) waits that long before the last line, writing the step lines first, so a tester can see a build in progress.
- **IMPLEMENT** `GET /images/json` with a `filters` query (`{"label":["k"]}` or `k=v`, same matching as `/containers/json`): answer `[{ Id, RepoTags: [name], Labels }]` for each stored image matching every label; images with the same Id are listed once with all their tags.
- **IMPLEMENT** `DELETE /images/<name or id>`: 404 if unknown; 409 `{ message: "conflict: unable to delete <name> (cannot be forced) - image is being used by running container <id>" }` if any container (running or not) has `Config.Image` equal to that name or that image's tag/id; else remove every tag of that image, 200 `[{"Deleted":"<id>"}]`.
- **IMPLEMENT** `GET /volumes` with label filters: `{ Volumes: [...], Warnings: null }`. `DELETE /volumes/<name>`: 404 if unknown; 409 `{ message: "remove <name>: volume is in use - [<container id>]" }` if any existing container has a mount with `Name === name`; else delete it, 204.
- **IMPLEMENT** in passive (non-exec) mode, a container whose `Cmd` is exactly `["true"]` exits at once with code 0 when started (call `exited(c, 0)` after marking it running) so `waitContainer` returns 0. Exec mode already runs `true` locally.
- **IMPLEMENT** expose `builds` (array) and `images` (the Map) on the object `startFakeDocker` returns, and add `builds` and `images` (as `[{ name, Id, Labels }]`) to `GET /__fake/state`. Update the `FakeDocker` type declaration that tests import (search for `FakeDocker` in `apps/graph-manager/scripts/`) with `builds: { tag: string; nocache: boolean; labels: Record<string, string>; dockerfile: string }[]` and the images map.
- **GOTCHA**: `handle()` parses every tar body before routing; `body.tarEntries` holds only names, so use the local `tarEntries` (with `data`) for the Dockerfile text. Existing tests rely on `imageExists` answering 404 for unknown names and on the `missing` pull failure — keep them green.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- docker` and `npm test -w graph-manager -- sandbox`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** tests against the fake:
  - `buildImage("gm-test:1", tarArchive([{ path: "Dockerfile", content: Buffer.from("FROM node:24\nRUN echo hi\n") }], { uid: 0, gid: 0 }), { labels: { "gm.sandbox-image": "1" }, nocache: true, onLine })` resolves; `onLine` got `Step 1/2 : FROM node:24` and `Successfully tagged gm-test:1`; `fake.builds[0]` has the tag, `nocache: true`, the labels and the Dockerfile text; `inspectImage("gm-test:1")` returns an `Id` starting with `sha256:` and `Config.Env` with a `PATH=` entry.
  - a Dockerfile containing `FAKE_BUILD_FAIL` rejects with a `DockerError` whose message is `fake build failed`, and `inspectImage` answers undefined.
  - `listImages("gm.sandbox-image")` lists the built image and not an image passed with `images: ["node:24"]`.
  - `removeImage` removes an unused image; a second call (404) and a call for an image used by a created container (409) both resolve without throwing, and the used image is still there.
  - `createVolume("v1", { "gm.clis": "1" })`, `listVolumes("gm.clis")` lists it, `removeVolume("v1")` removes it; removing a volume mounted by a container resolves and keeps it.
  - a container created with `Cmd: ["true"]` and started returns 0 from `waitContainer`.
- **PATTERN**: the existing tests in `docker.test.ts` (fake per test, closed in `afterEach`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- docker.test`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DockerClient` has `buildImage`, `inspectImage`, `listImages`, `removeImage`, `listVolumes`, `removeVolume`, and `createVolume(name, labels?)`, as above.
- [ ] `buildImage` streams log lines to `onLine` while the build runs and throws `DockerError` with Docker's `errorDetail.message` when the stream reports an error.
- [ ] `removeImage` and `removeVolume` treat 404 and 409 as success.
- [ ] The fake supports `POST /build` (with `FAKE_BUILD_FAIL` and `--build-delay`), image inspect/list/delete, volume list/delete, `Cmd: ["true"]` containers exiting 0, and exposes `builds` and `images`.
- [ ] All existing graph-manager tests still pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- docker
npm test -w graph-manager
```
